title: Codec Tokenizer Map
description: A per-model dialect for the Codec binary transport protocol. Carries the data needed to encode text into token IDs (BPETokenizer / LongestMatchTokenizer) and decode IDs back to text (Detokenizer). Maps are content-addressed and immutable — a new model version publishes a new map at a new URL with a new sha256 hash.

id.description: Stable, globally unique tokenizer identifier (convention: lowercase 'org/model-family', e.g. 'meta-llama/llama-3'). Same ID + same hash means byte-identical map.

version.description: Schema version. '2' for the current schema (vocab + merges + encoder). '1' for legacy maps that use the 'tokens' field instead of 'vocab'. Implementations SHOULD accept both for backwards compatibility.

vocab_size.description: Total number of token IDs in the vocabulary. Valid IDs are 0 … vocab_size-1.

vocab.description: Vocabulary as { raw_token_text: id }. 'Raw' means the form stored in HuggingFace tokenizer.json — for byte_level encoding this contains GPT-2-encoded characters (Ġ, etc.); for metaspace it contains ▁-prefixed strings. The Detokenizer applies the appropriate decoder. Required for v2 maps.

tokens.description: DEPRECATED — legacy v1 vocabulary as { id_string: decoded_text }. Present only on v1 maps. New maps use 'vocab' instead.

encoder.description:
How vocab tokens are encoded:
  byte_level — GPT-2 byte→unicode mapping (Llama-3, Qwen, Phi-3, DeepSeek-V3, Mistral-Nemo, Falcon, SmolLM2, Codestral byte_level variants).
  metaspace  — ▁ as space prefix, SentencePiece-style (Llama-2, Mistral-v3, Mixtral, Gemma).
Omitted on identity / vocab-only maps where tokens are already decoded text.

merges.description: BPE merges in priority order (lower index = higher priority). Each entry is two tokens separated by a single space, e.g. 'Ġ a'. Required by BPETokenizer for client-side encoding. Absent for vocab-only / canonical-IR maps that use only LongestMatchTokenizer.

pre_tokenizer_pattern.description: Regex pattern that splits input text into pieces before byte-encoding and BPE merging. Required by BPETokenizer when encoder = 'byte_level' AND pre_tokenizer_program is absent. The pattern uses Unicode property classes (\p{L}, \p{N}, …) which all major regex engines support.

pre_tokenizer_program.description: v2.1: compiled pre-tokenizer program — an ordered op list runtimes can execute without a Unicode regex engine. Preferred over pre_tokenizer_pattern when both are present. See spec/PRETOKENIZER_PROGRAM.md for the full op set and equivalence rules.

byte_fallback_start.description: First token ID in the byte-fallback range (inclusive). IDs in [byte_fallback_start, byte_fallback_end] represent raw UTF-8 bytes 0x00–0xFF and are accumulated by the Detokenizer until they form a valid UTF-8 sequence. SentencePiece-derived tokenizers only.

byte_fallback_end.description: Last token ID in the byte-fallback range (inclusive).

special_tokens.description: Named special token IDs (e.g. '<|endoftext|>', '<|im_start|>'). Skipped during text rendering by default; opt in via Detokenizer renderSpecial option.

published_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when this map was published. Informational only — content addressing is via sha256 hash, not timestamp.

zstd_dictionaries.description: Optional pre-trained ZSTD dictionaries for compressing CodecFrame streams emitted by this model. One entry per Codec wire format (msgpack, protobuf) — they train against different byte distributions and are not interchangeable. A server that loads the dict for a given format compresses every frame in the stream against it; a client that loads the same dict (matched by hash) decompresses with it. Dicts are content-addressed by sha256; a new training run publishes a new entry with a new hash. Servers and clients SHOULD fetch the dict once and cache it indefinitely.

format.description: Codec wire format this dictionary was trained against. Servers MUST select the dict whose format matches the response's stream_format; using a mismatched dict is a wire-format error.

url.description: URL the dictionary file can be fetched from. Typically a CDN or GitHub raw URL. The body MUST be the raw zstd dictionary bytes (the output of zstd --train or zstandard.train_dictionary), not a JSON wrapper.

hash.description: sha256 of the dictionary file body, prefixed with 'sha256:'. Implementations MUST verify the fetched bytes match this hash before loading.

size_bytes.description: Size of the dictionary file in bytes. Informational; aids cache budgeting.

trained_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when this dictionary was trained. Informational only.

corpus_summary.description: Free-form metadata about the training corpus (sample count, source kind, prompt-shape mix). Helpful for downstream auditors deciding whether to re-train.
